subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm picturing a four-wheeled armored police interceptor with a roof-mounted water cannon turret and neon light bars, styled like a cyberpunk corpo security vehicle in black, white, and red with cyan and magenta accents. A static model should work fine since there's no creature skeleton required.

I'll build it from boxes, extrudes, and glow elements, using SVG textures for decals like corp logos, hazard stripes, and "RIOT CONTROL" text, and I'll skip joints since this is a static prop without moving parts like wheel rotation or a turret hinge. I'm planning a custom paint shader for the body with countershading and grime buildup near the wheels, pulling from the SDK's paint, mix, noise, and smoothstep utilities rather than using a prebuilt kit.

Now I'm working out the hull geometry -- setting wheel radius and axle height, body width, and the chassis box dimensions, then sketching the side profile points for an extruded hull with a sloped hood, windshield, cabin roof, and flat rear.

I'm also figuring out dark fender flares over the wheel wells, since cutting the body isn't straightforward -- I'll add thin dark boxes to simulate wheel arches and adjust wheel position so they sit properly against the body width.

Then I'm working out the wheels themselves: a rotated cylinder for tire shape, with a smaller inner cylinder for the hub and possibly a neon ring accent for a cyber aesthetic.

Working out the windshield tilt angle so the glass slopes correctly, computing the rotation needed and positioning it slightly offset along the surface normal with a dark cyan-tinted glass material.

Now I'm planning the side cab windows as separate planes mounted on the x-faces, figuring out their z-range to match the roof's sloped region near the windshield base.

For side decals, I'm working out texture orientation so the artwork reads correctly when viewed from outside the vehicle, reasoning through which direction is "right" relative to the viewer facing each face.

Now I'm designing the roof details: a cyberpunk light bar alternating cyan and red emissive segments, plus a rear water cannon turret with a rotating base and barrel, noting the barrel path forward would conflict with the light bar's position.

I'll offset the turret pivot higher and tilt the tapered barrel upward so it clears the light bar, adding a nozzle flare and a glowing gauge, then adding a horizontal cylindrical water tank blister on the rear roof in translucent cyan.

For the tank, I'm going with a pale blue cylinder with white stripe decals instead of transparency, connected to the turret by a dark rubber hose sweep. The front gets a heavy push bumper with red neon strips, slim glowing headlight slits, and an invented corporate decal like "MERIDIAN" since I want to avoid using real brand names like Arasaka.

I'm settling on "HELIX-9 CROWD SUPPRESSION" as the fictional corp name, designing a hex emblem logo with hazard stripes and a "NON-LETHAL*" warning for the side panel texture. Now I'm building the front bumper geometry as a box with an angled prod bar, plus a push plow extrusion.

For the plow I'm shaping a trapezoid profile with painted hazard stripes, then moving to side details like door lines, handles, armor plates, a shield rack, spotlights, and mesh grille windows, finishing with rear doors, a glowing tail light bar, exhaust, sensors, and a "STAND BACK" warning light.

Now I'm adding a glowing amber "DISPERSE" LED sign on the rear and cyan/magenta neon underglow strips along the sills, plus a roof antenna array with red-tipped rods, a camera dome, glowing mirror indicators, siren cube rows, front grille slats with neon accents, a hood vent, and a small license plate texture, all tying into a cyberpunk yellow/cyan aesthetic.

For the body paint, I'm defining a procedural shader that blends dark charcoal and white tones using noise, darkening toward the bottom edge to simulate grime, then adding a thin cyan stripe band near the lower hull.

I'm also setting up panel seam lines on the side faces using a modulo pattern along the z-axis, and deciding to import only the glow kit to minimize risk while keeping the flat color palette small. Now I'm starting to define the box-building helper function for constructing the model.

Writing box helper...

I'm planning out the texture list needed for the model—livery sides, rear sign, windshield, logos, headlamp, and HUD dome—and beginning to sketch the SVG for the side livery.

The decal edges stay within the flat face region since bevel only rounds outline rims, so the panel placement is safe. Now I'm positioning the side window glass with reflection, sizing it to fit between the cab pillar slope and roofline so it doesn't clip into the windshield or roof geometry.

For the livery strip, I need to shift its center from -0.9 to -1.1 to avoid overlapping the window region, keeping its span within the rear fender limit while maintaining the height around the door seam area. Next I'll work out the front grille placement on the lower profile.

Mapping the front face slope from the hood line down to the bumper edge, I plan to position headlight boxes near the center height, sinking them slightly into the sloped surface so they sit flush rather than floating in front of it. Then I'll add a plow/bumper extrusion along the lower front edge.

Defining plow outline coordinates...

I'm adding a hazard-stripe diagonal pattern for the lower band and a neon red glow strip on the plow's front face, then starting on the roof light bar as a dark base box with alternating segments.

Now I'm positioning the roof gear elements — end caps for the light bar, a turret pedestal cylinder, and sketching a lathe profile for the dome shape.

Still shaping the barrel geometry and nozzle lathe profile, then adding a pressure hose tube connecting the tank to the turret with a catmull sweep.

Now I'm positioning the horizontal fuel tank cylinder with rounded end caps, pale blue-grey coloring, a glowing cyan level window strip on its front face, and reinforcing bands at each end, plus setting up a base cradle to hold it in place.

Next I'm adding antenna rods with glowing red tips, a hemisphere camera dome with a cyan lens glow on the front roof, and small beacon lights at the roof corners, then placing a rear sign plane.

For the back of the vehicle, I'm positioning a glowing rear panel, door seam details with hinges, red glow tail light boxes, a dark rear bumper, exhaust cylinders, and a rear step, all oriented to face backward correctly.

Now I'm building the side details: an underglow strip with cyan glow, a dark sill, fender flares, a livery plane with window and door seams, a mirror assembly with amber accent, and a neon side stripe.

Adding mesh cage bars, spotlight pillars, and armor plates toward the rear lower half instead of full shield props.

I'm also sizing wheel arch flares to sit above the wheel tops without clipping, with extra side wall boxes for a rounded flare cap near the fenders.

Wheel overlap with body edge looks typical and acceptable. I'm adding a dark undercarriage box plus axle rods at the wheel centers, then thinking about paint seams and a roof decal reading "H9-07" — I need to fix the plane's up vector since facing straight up creates a degenerate orientation with the default axis.

For the roof decal, I'll set up to [0,0,1] so the text top leans toward the front, readable from above while facing forward. I'm skipping the roof placement for now in favor of adding markings on the hood instead, though the hood's sloped surface means I'd need to tilt the plane — deciding to simplify and just add a front plate texture instead.

Adding a license plate on the plow with "H9-07" text, positioned above the glow strip, and keeping tires a flat matte color with steel hubs rather than modeling individual tread blocks, maybe adding a thin magenta glow ring decal on the sidewall for visual interest.

I'm positioning hub caps and bolt rings around the wheel using angular loops, then estimating the total part count lands around 200, which seems reasonable. Now I'm setting up the cyberpunk color palette with cyan, magenta, red, yellow, and amber accents against a light body color.

Writing SVG livery code...

I'm designing the rear warning sign with amber glowing text on black, then working out how to place water droplet decals on the tank's flat end caps using small planes instead of spheres to keep the geometry simple.

I'm also planning the full texture set—side, windshield, rear, drop, plate, a warning triangle decal, and a glowing slit-style headlight—then starting to extrude the hull shape from its outline profile.

Mapping out the hull's outline coordinates now, making sure the polygon points trace around the body without crossing over themselves.

For paint zones, I'm planning the dark charcoal lower hull versus white upper front hood, plus some roof ribs as small boxes to add detail without colliding with the turret mount.

I'm also sketching door seam lines as thin dark boxes flanking the cab door, plus a small steel handle box positioned near the window opening.

Now I'm adding window cage bars as a few evenly spaced thin boxes across the opening, then moving on to the front light bar and grille slats with headlamps positioned on either side of a central grille section.

I'm also working on placing a hex-logo emblem on the hood's sloped front face, checking its position and size against the plow geometry so they don't visually overlap.

Next I'm placing the headlights as glowing planes with angled normals matching the hood slope, sized and positioned to sit above the plow, and adding dark housing boxes behind them for depth.

I'll skip the roof spotlight pods, define a helper for textured planes with optional up-vector for top-down placement, and make sure wheel bottoms sit exactly at ground level with no clipping. Then I'll write the final code, starting with the hazard stripe paint color.

Writing plow paint logic...
